arson bomb investigator.why: Delta has NO fire technology program and no fire service courses. The only fire-named course in the catalog is ELEC 41 Fire Alarm Systems, which is an electrical installation course, not fire service training.

Two options to put to the college: refer these students to Modesto Junior College (265 career credentials, the largest portfolio in the state), or treat a Delta fire program as a strategic build. MAP does flag Delta as a potential adopter on Firefighter 1 and Fire Apparatus Driver/Operator 1B, which means the platform expects a college of Delta's profile to offer it.

readme: What this is

A working agenda for one conversation: which of {college}'s existing courses, programs and certificates could carry Credit for Prior Learning (CPL) for the occupations on the {partner} occupation list — and which of those already have a credit-recommendation exhibit built in the MAP platform.
It narrows the earlier statewide SJCOE crosswalk (August 2026, {n} occupations across all 116 colleges) down to what {college} itself has available.
The headline
• {college} has adopted ZERO CPL exhibits for any occupation on this list. Its only career/technical CPL today is POST Basic Academy; the other 68 exhibits it carries are AP and CLEP exams.

• Yet it has a confirmed matching offering for {nC} of the {n} occupations — and for {n1} of those, the MAP exhibit ALREADY EXISTS and lists the college as a potential adopter. The curriculum is there and the exhibit is there; only the articulation is missing.

• It also appears to hold curriculum for the hydro/utility occupations that have NO credit recommendation anywhere in California ({n2} of them). That is a first-in-state build opportunity, not a catch-up one.

• It has no fire technology instruction at all, which is the single largest cluster on the list (17 occupations) and the best-covered cluster statewide. Those students need a referral or a college build.
How to read the columns
Alignment status — the three categories requested, based on the COLLEGE'S OFFERING only:
Confirmed alignment  ·  An active program or named course sequence teaches this occupation's core content.
Potential — validate with college  ·  Partial or adjacent coverage; a faculty member needs to confirm.
No apparent alignment  ·  Nothing in the active catalog covers this.
MAP exhibit status — a separate question: does a credit-recommendation exhibit already exist, and where does the college stand on it?
"flagged as potential adopter" means MAP already identifies this college as one that could adopt. These are the cheapest wins.
"No CPL exhibit anywhere" means nothing exists statewide — a build, and often a chance to be first.
Priority — derived from those two columns, not authored. See the Priority Opportunities tab.
Method (same as the original SJCOE crosswalk)
Occupation → credential matching is reused verbatim from the shared map built for the first SJCOE run (kb/occupation_credential_map.json, {n} occupations / 406 rulings). Nothing was re-judged there.

Occupation → college offering matching is NEW subject-matter judgment for this run, made against the COCI program export and the published course catalog. It is a discussion agenda, not a determination — faculty decide what articulates.
MAP exhibit status is read mechanically from the MAP adoption data; no judgment involved.

Caveats worth saying out loud in the meeting
Program and course data is a point-in-time export; the college may have added or retired offerings since. Confirm anything you act on.
A course-title match is not a curriculum review. Every "confirmed" row still needs the discipline faculty to agree the learning outcomes line up.
Adopter counts here union statewide adoptions and local articulations, so they can legitimately exceed the count shown on MAP's Statewide Exhibits view.

The plumbing apprenticeship (A CON 87A–90D) does not sit under a plumbing-named program in COCI, so it is invisible to a program search. There may be other pathways the same is true of — worth asking directly.
